subject: english
question:
Directions: Each item in this section has a sentence with three underlined parts labelled as (a), (b) and (c). Read each sentence to find out whether there is any error in any underlined part and indicate your response on the answer sheet against the corresponding letter, i.e., (a) or (b) or (c). If you find no error, your response should be indicated as (d).

__The newly admitted students could not__(a)/__access the library because they had__(b)/__not yet been given their ID cards__(c)/__No Error__(d)
solution:
The correct answer is ‘**Option 2**’.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The error in the sentence lies in the tense used. The past perfect tense ‘**had**’ is used incorrectly in the context of the sentence.
 
• "**Yet**" is typically used with the present perfect tense in negative and interrogative sentences to refer to actions up to the present moment.
 
• Hence, '**had**' will be replaced by the verb '**have**' because the noun '**students**' is plural.
 
• The sentence is talking about a present situation (students not being able to access the library) that is a result of a past action (not receiving ID cards).

Therefore, the correct answer is ‘**Option 2**’.

 

**Correct Sentence**: “The newly admitted students could not **access the library because they have** not yet been given their ID cards.”

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1**: There is no error in part (a) of the sentence. ‘**The newly admitted students**’ is grammatically correct.
 
• **Option 3**: There is no error in part (c) of the sentence. ‘**not yet been given their ID cards**’ is grammatically correct.
 
• **Option 4**: This option suggests that there is no error in the sentence, which is incorrect as explained above.
